- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or slowly rising, adjust upward by 2–5% to account for sentiment-driven momentum.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days to avoid overshoot.  
- If official supply net is negative and sentiment is bearish, model underestimates downside risk; add 3–8% downward bias to forecast mean.  
- When sentiment swings from bullish to bearish within 3–5 days, model often lags; shift forecast downward by 1–3% per day of lag.  
- In high-event periods (≥20 events/30d), model tends to overestimate volatility; cap forecast range within ±3% of recent 7-day moving average.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated bearish spikes (e.g., 3+ days of -0.5 to 0.0), model often fails to anticipate reversal; add 1–2% upward bias to next 3–5 days.  
- For long-term (30d) forecasts, if recent 18-day mean is rising, model often underestimates peak; add 1–3% upward bias to forecast peak.  
- If official events show net bearish supply and no policy intervention, model often underestimates downside; apply 2–5% downward bias to forecast mean.
